description: Fix the real, safe security issue found in the audit (FEAT-001): the DOM-XSS attribute-injection in the maps-rating modal in html/js/front.js, where GCPD-scraped map name and skill_group are interpolated into innerHTML (text nodes and alt/title attributes) without HTML escaping. The fix must NOT change any application behavior for legitimate data (map names, skill-group labels, win/tie/loss counts, rank icons, tooltips must render exactly as before for normal Steam data) - it only neutralizes hostile characters. Prefer the lowest-risk, most testable approach: introduce a small pure HTML-escaping helper and either (a) build the maps-modal rows with DOM APIs (createElement + textContent + setAttribute) instead of an innerHTML template string, or (b) escape every interpolated scraped value with the helper before it enters the innerHTML template. Approach (a) is the most robust and is preferred if it can be done without altering the rendered markup/columns; approach (b) is acceptable if it keeps the markup byte-identical for safe input. The escaping helper should live where it is unit-testable (e.g. a pure function exported from a helpers/ module, or a pure top-level function in front.js mirrored by a testable helper) so a regression test can assert it neutralizes attribute-breakout payloads. Additionally, harden showToast (front.js:43) ONLY for the dynamic call sites that interpolate non-static data (login + ret.error): keep the intentional static-HTML toast (the 'download it here' update link) working, but ensure error/login text cannot inject markup - the cleanest option is to escape the interpolated dynamic substrings at those specific call sites using the same helper, without converting the whole showToast to textContent (which would break the intentional link toast). Do NOT touch EncryptedStorage crypto, GC/rank invariants, protoDecode, or the changelog markdown-it path.
steps: Add a small, pure, unit-testable HTML-escaping helper. Recommended: create helpers/htmlEscape.js exporting `escapeHtml(value)` that coerces to string and replaces & < > " ' with their HTML entities (& < > " '), returning '' for null/undefined. Keep it dependency-free and documented with a SECURITY NOTE explaining it neutralizes attribute-breakout from GCPD-scraped data.

Expose the escape helper to the renderer. Options: require it in preload.js and expose via contextBridge (e.g. window.htmlEscape.escape) mirroring the existing md_converter/fastEqual pattern, OR define an identical pure escapeHtml at the top of html/js/front.js (renderer has no module system; rankFormat.js-style global). Choose the approach that is testable AND keeps behavior identical. If defining it in front.js, ALSO put the same logic in helpers/htmlEscape.js so it can be unit-tested; document that they must stay in sync (or, preferably, expose the single helpers/htmlEscape.js implementation through preload so there is one source of truth).

Fix the '.show-maps' handler in html/js/front.js (~L1025-1055): rebuild each map row so scraped mapName and mapData.skill_group can never inject markup. Preferred: construct cells with document.createElement + textContent for the map name, wins, ties, losses, and last-match cells, and set the img src/alt/title via setAttribute (which does not parse HTML). If keeping the innerHTML template, wrap EVERY interpolated scraped value (mapName in the alt attribute and the name cell, skill_group in the alt and title attributes) in escapeHtml(...). The numeric fields (wins/ties/losses/region) are Number.parseInt results and safe, but escaping them is harmless. getRankImage/getMapIconPath outputs are app-controlled paths; keep as-is. Ensure the rendered result for a normal map name like 'Dust II' and a skill_group like 'Silver I' is visually/structurally identical to before.

Harden the dynamic showToast call sites in html/js/front.js that pass interpolated non-static data: `showToast(login + ': ' + ret.error, 'danger')` (~L629, L795, L810). Escape the login and error substrings with escapeHtml before concatenation so a hostile error/login string cannot inject markup, while leaving the intentional static-HTML update-link toast (~L862) unchanged. Do NOT convert showToast itself to textContent.

Add regression tests. Create test/htmlEscape.test.js (node:test) asserting escapeHtml: escapes < > & " ', handles null/undefined -> '', leaves benign strings unchanged, and specifically neutralizes an attribute-breakout payload like `x" onerror="alert(1)` (the ambient exploit) so the quote becomes " and no raw quote survives. If the renderer maps-row building is refactored into a pure helper (e.g. a function that returns the escaped attribute string or builds a row given a document), add a focused test for that too. Keep tests free of any real Steam credentials/network.
Run `node --check` on every edited .js file (html/js/front.js, preload.js if edited, helpers/htmlEscape.js).
Run the full verification suite and confirm nothing regressed.
acceptance_criteria: A pure escapeHtml helper exists and is unit-tested; test/htmlEscape.test.js passes and includes a case proving the attribute-breakout payload `x" onerror="alert(1)` has its double-quote escaped to " (no raw `"` survives).

The '.show-maps' maps-modal handler no longer interpolates unescaped scraped mapName/skill_group into innerHTML: either it builds rows via createElement/textContent/setAttribute, or every scraped value is passed through escapeHtml before entering the template.
For legitimate data (e.g. map 'Dust II', skill_group 'Silver Elite'), the maps modal renders the same columns/values/icons/tooltips as before (no behavior change for normal Steam data).
Dynamic showToast call sites that interpolate login/ret.error escape those substrings; the intentional static-HTML update-link toast still renders its link.
`npm test` passes with MORE tests than the 133 baseline (new htmlEscape tests) and 0 failures.
`npm run lint` is clean; `npm audit` is 0 vulnerabilities; `npm run package` builds dist/linux-unpacked.
No changes to EncryptedStorage crypto, GC/rank/XP invariants, protoDecode, or the markdown-it changelog path; the front.js wins_dz asymmetry and DOM write order are untouched.
verification: Run `npm test` and confirm >=134 pass / 0 fail (baseline 133 + new htmlEscape tests).
Run `npm run lint` and confirm clean.
Run `npm run package` and confirm dist/linux-unpacked is produced (Windows wine failure is expected, not a regression).
Run `node --check html/js/front.js`, `node --check helpers/htmlEscape.js`, and `node --check preload.js` (if edited) and confirm all pass.
Manually re-read the '.show-maps' handler to confirm no unescaped scraped value reaches innerHTML.
